# daylight_server

> GPU annual daylight and solar simulation on meshes over HTTP (kit-sim_daylight core: OptiX ray tracing,
> Radiance-derived Perez sky, validated against Ladybug Tools, Radiance and pvlib). Several users share one GPU
> through a job queue.

The complete, machine-readable description is the OpenAPI 3.1 document at /openapi.json (human views: /docs, /redoc).
Read it for every parameter, schema, example and error. Operation ids: uploadMesh, meshExists, submitJob, getJob,
cancelJob, listMyJobs, runSync, proxyDownload, getHealth. Agent routes (--mcp, this machine only): mcpMessage, mcpGet,
bridgeNext, bridgeResult, readLocalPath, listReports, saveReport, deleteReport, printReport, getReportPdf, getSession,
putSession, deleteSession.

## Workflow

1. PUT /mesh/{id} with one .dmesh image per mesh (id: your UUID; layout in uploadMesh, optionally with one uint16
   optics slot per face, header flags bit 0). Upload once; meshes stay cached. ?name= names it in results and --optics.
2. POST /jobs (multipart/form-data): `sensors` = receiving mesh ids (repeat the field), `context` = shading-only mesh
   ids, `args` = CLI flags, one token per field (e.g. --lat 52.52 --lon 13.41 --tz 1 --quantity radiation,sunhours),
   weather = an `epw` file part, an `epw_url`, or the --clear-sky flag. 404 {"missing": [...]}: upload those, resubmit.
3. GET /jobs/{id}?wait=25 until `state` is done, error or cancelled (each call returns early when something changes).
4. done: `values_b64` = base64 float64 little-endian, row-major [sum(meshes[].count) x columns.length]; rows of mesh k
   are meshes[k].first .. first+count-1, one per face (per vertex with --on vertices) in upload order.
5. DELETE /jobs/{id} cancels. POST /run = steps 2-4 in one blocking call.

## Conventions

- Mesh coordinates: metres, Z up, right-handed winding; the face normal is the front side.
- Units: radiation, direct, diffuse kWh/m2 over the period; irradiance W/m2 mean; illuminance lux mean; sunhours h.
  direct = beam x transmittance; sunhours = equivalent full-sun hours (an hour behind tau 0.6 counts 0.6; an exact
  count while every surface is opaque, the default). With --bounces > 0, radiation, diffuse, irradiance and
  illuminance include the light reflected by the model; direct and sunhours never do.
- Surfaces: opaque and black by default; numbers only, no materials. --optics NAME[/SLOT]=RHO[,TAU[,glass|porous]]
  (repeatable, ';' packs several in one token, * = every mesh; NAME/SLOT > NAME > * > built-in rho 0.2 tau 0; 0..1,
  rho + tau <= 1, glass: rho 0 and 0 < tau <= 0.918; porous when tau > 0 unless glass). --transmission on (physical
  mode only; ladybug refuses it) lets tau through; --fresnel off makes glass pass tau at every angle and, with
  --bounces, mirror nothing (default on: both by angle).
- Reflected light: --bounces N (0..20, default 0 = none; physical mode only, ladybug refuses N > 0) adds up to N
  diffuse reflections by each slot's rho (unused without it: every surface black); 1 for outdoor studies, 5-8 for
  interiors. --bounce-samples M (64..65536, default 1024) paths per sensor: time linear in M (at 1024 about 2 s more
  per million sensors on a city-like model, RTX 2060), noise ~1 / sqrt(M) (at 1024 annual facade values 0.5 % median,
  2.3 % p95; a single --time instant 2.3 % / 14 %: use 4096-16384 for instants and small differences).
- cache.scene: reused = the scene was still on the GPU. A scene = the sensors ids then the context ids, in order,
  --no-self-occlude, and the layout of the slots that cast shade: the set that transmits (tau > 0 with --transmission
  on), else with --bounces > 0 and a quantity other than direct / sunhours whether their rho or glass differ (with
  --fresnel off none is glass; a hit record per slot). New --optics values reuse it while that layout stays; a slot
  that starts or stops transmitting, or --bounces switched on or off (with such a quantity) for a model whose slots
  differ (none transmitting), is another scene (built, then kept).
- Columns: <quantity>_<side>, e.g. radiation_front.
- Time (standard time, no DST): annual by default; --time MM-DDTHH:MM one instant; --from TS --to TS --step MIN a
  range (the sun at the middle of each step); add --hours HH:MM-HH:MM for only those hours of every day (e.g.
  09:00-17:00 from 06-01 to 08-31). --tz is the clock of these times (default: the EPW's zone); an EPW keeps its own
  zone and the times are moved into it, so send the site's civil standard offset.
- Weather: needed for every quantity except sunhours. Nearest measured station: GET /proxy with the EnergyPlus index
  URL (see proxyDownload); any location: a PVGIS TMY URL as epw_url.

## Limits

- Errors are text/plain, first line "error: <cause>"; 400 = usage (with the CLI usage text), 500 = runtime. An
  --optics row naming no mesh of the run (or several), a slot out of range or a row given twice fails the job (state
  error, status 500), not the submission.
- Send X-Client-Id to identify your client: at most 2 jobs queued or running per client (429), 32 in the queue (503),
  both with Retry-After. Finished jobs are kept 15 minutes. Identical requests are answered from a result cache.
- No authentication; job ids are random UUIDs only their submitter knows.

## Agents (MCP)

With --mcp, an agent on this machine works with the web app itself instead of the routes above: it opens models by
path, sets roles, settings and cameras, runs, reads results and critical areas, takes screenshots of any size, edits
charts, writes PDF reports (one option, or 2-4 compared) and discusses what the results mean.
- Endpoint: POST /mcp (mcpMessage), JSON-RPC over HTTP, revisions 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26, JSON answers
  (no SSE). Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http daylight http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp (if it does not connect,
  set MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy). Claude Desktop: the stdio relay server/mcp-stdio.mjs, with an absolute node.exe
  path in claude_desktop_config.json.
- Start with the app_state tool; tools/list describes every tool. Each call answers within 55 s: "running" or
  "generating" means call it again.
- Calls run in the app's browser tab (keep it open) or, with none open, in a hidden instance the server starts (--web
  or --app-url); opening the app picks that session up.
- Agent routes answer only requests from this machine (403) and are off without --mcp (404).
